title.zh: 卷437 列傳二百二十四 荣禄 王文韶 张之洞 瞿鸿禨
title.en: Volume 437 Biographies 224: Rong Lu, Wang Wenshao, Zhang Zhidong, Qu Hongji
title.raw: 卷437 列傳二百二十四 荣禄 王文韶 张之洞 瞿鸿禨

sentences.zh: 榮祿，字仲華，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Rong Lu, style name Zhonghua, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu, styled Zhonghua, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and came from the Manchu Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖喀什噶爾幫辦大臣塔斯哈，父總兵長壽，均見忠義傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tasgha, assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, a regional commander, are both recorded in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tasgha, who had served as assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, a regional commander, both have biographies in the Loyalty and Righteousness section.

sentences.zh: 榮祿以廕生賞主事，隸工部，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: Rong Lu, through hereditary privilege, was granted the post of secretary and was attached to the Ministry of Works, later promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: By virtue of hereditary privilege Rong Lu received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of Works and was later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸候補道。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as an expectant circuit intendant in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He then left the capital to serve as an expectant circuit intendant in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 同治初，設神機營，賞五品京堂，充翼長，兼專操大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign the Shenji Camp was established; he was granted the rank of fifth-grade capital official, served as wing commander, and concurrently held the post of drill commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, when the Shenji Camp was founded, he was given fifth-rank capital status, appointed wing commander, and made drill commissioner as well.

sentences.zh: 再遷左翼總兵。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to commander of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again, to commander of the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 用大學士文祥薦，改工部侍郎，調戶部，兼總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Wenxiang, he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Works, then moved to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently served as superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Grand Secretary Wenxiang, he became vice minister of Works, was transferred to Revenue, and also served as superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 穆宗崩，德宗嗣統。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Tongzhi died, Emperor Guangxu ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 榮祿言於恭親王，乃請頒詔，俟嗣皇帝有子，承繼穆宗。

translations.literal: Rong Lu spoke to Prince Gong, and thus a decree was requested proclaiming that when the succeeding emperor had a son, that son would inherit Muzong's line.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu urged Prince Gong to seek an edict stipulating that when the new emperor had a son, that heir would continue Emperor Tongzhi's succession line.

sentences.zh: 其後始定以紹統者為嗣。

translations.literal: Only afterward was it settled that the one who succeeded to the unified throne should be designated heir.
translations.idiomatic: Only later was it decided that the emperor who had inherited the unified throne would himself be named as heir.

sentences.zh: ，兼步軍統領。

translations.literal: He also concurrently served as commander of the Metropolitan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He also held the concurrent post of commander of the Metropolitan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 遷左都御史，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left censor-in-chief and promoted to minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left censor-in-chief and then promoted to minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 慈禧皇太后嘗欲自選宮監，榮祿奏非祖制，忤旨。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Cixi once wished to choose palace eunuchs herself; Rong Lu memorialized that this was not ancestral institution and thereby offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cixi once wanted to select palace eunuchs on her own; Rong Lu submitted that this violated established practice and thus fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 會學士寶廷奏言滿大臣兼差多，乃解尚書及內務府差。

translations.literal: When Academician Baoting memorialized that Manchu grand ministers held too many concurrent posts, Rong Lu was relieved of his ministries and his post in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Academician Baoting reported that Manchu ministers were holding too many concurrent offices, Rong Lu was stripped of his ministry posts and his Imperial Household appointment.

sentences.zh: 又以被劾納賄，降二級，旋開復，出為西安將軍。

translations.literal: He was also impeached for taking bribes, demoted two ranks, soon restored, and sent out as military governor of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of accepting bribes, he was demoted two ranks, soon reinstated, and then sent out as military governor of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 二十年，祝嘏留京，再授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he remained in the capital for the birthday felicitations and was again appointed commander of the Metropolitan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of the reign he stayed in the capital for the imperial birthday celebrations and was again made commander of the Metropolitan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 日本構釁，恭親王、慶親王督辦軍務，榮祿參其事。

translations.literal: When Japan provoked hostilities, Princes Gong and Qing supervised military affairs, and Rong Lu took part in them.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out with Japan, Princes Gong and Qing were put in charge of military affairs, and Rong Lu assisted them.

sentences.zh: 和議成，疏薦溫處道袁世凱練新軍，是曰「新建陸軍」。

translations.literal: After peace was concluded, he memorialized recommending Circuit Intendant Yuan Shikai of Wenzhou to drill a new army, which was then called the "Newly Created Army."
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was settled, he recommended Circuit Intendant Yuan Shikai to train a new army—the force later known as the Newly Created Army.

sentences.zh: 授兵部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of the Ministry of War and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of War and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏請益練新軍，而調甘肅提督董福祥軍入衛京師。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting further training of the new army and the transfer of Gansu Provincial Commander Dong Fuxiang's troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He urged expanded training for the new army and brought Gansu Provincial Commander Dong Fuxiang's forces into the capital as guards.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，晉大學士，命為直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to grand secretary and appointed governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the reign he became a grand secretary and was appointed governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 是時上擢用主事康有為及知府譚嗣同等參預新政，議變法，斥舊臣，召直隸按察使袁世凱入覲，超授侍郎，統練兵。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor promoted and employed the secretary Kang Youwei and the prefect Tan Sitong and others to participate in the new policies, discussed reform, dismissed old ministers, summoned Zhili Provincial Judge Yuan Shikai to audience, granted him extraordinary promotion to vice minister, and put him in charge of training troops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then elevated Secretary Kang Youwei, Prefect Tan Sitong, and others to help run the New Policies, debated institutional reform, and sidelined the old guard; he summoned Zhili Provincial Judge Yuan Shikai, promoted him directly to vice minister, and placed him in command of military training.

sentences.zh: 榮祿不自安，御史楊崇伊奏請太后再垂簾，於是太后复臨朝訓政，召榮祿為軍機大臣，以世凱代之，命查拿康有為，斬譚嗣同等六人於市，以上有疾，詔徵醫；

translations.literal: Rong Lu felt ill at ease; Censor Yang Chongyi memorialized asking the Empress Dowager to resume the curtain regency; thereupon the Empress Dowager again held court behind the curtain and directed government, summoned Rong Lu as a Grand Councilor, replaced him with Yuan Shikai, ordered the arrest of Kang Youwei, executed Tan Sitong and five others in the marketplace, and because the emperor was ill, issued an edict summoning physicians;
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy at these developments, Rong Lu backed Censor Yang Chongyi's plea for the Empress Dowager to resume regency; Cixi again took up rule from behind the curtain, recalled Rong Lu to the Grand Council, sent Yuan Shikai to replace him in Zhili, ordered Kang Youwei seized, and had Tan Sitong and five others executed in public—while an edict, citing the emperor's illness, called for physicians.

sentences.zh: 復命榮祿管兵部，仍節制北洋海陸各軍。

translations.literal: Rong Lu was again ordered to administer the Ministry of War and still to command all Beiyang naval and land forces.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu was again put in charge of the Ministry of War and retained overall command of Beiyang's land and naval forces.

sentences.zh: 榮祿乃奏設武衛軍，以聶士成駐蘆臺為前軍，董福祥駐薊州為後軍，宋慶駐山海關為左軍，世凱駐小站為右軍，而自募萬人為中軍，駐南苑。

translations.literal: Rong Lu then memorialized to establish the Wuyi Army: Nie Shicheng stationed at Lutai as the Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as the Rear Army, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as the Left Army, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as the Right Army, while he himself recruited ten thousand men as the Central Army, stationed at the Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu then proposed the Wuyi Army: Nie Shicheng's Front Army at Lutai, Dong Fuxiang's Rear Army at Jizhou, Song Qing's Left Army at Shanhaiguan, Yuan Shikai's Right Army at Xiaozhan, and a Central Army of ten thousand men he raised himself, camped at the Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 時太后議廢帝，立端王載漪子溥俊為穆宗嗣，患外人為梗，用榮祿言，改稱「大阿哥」。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager deliberated on deposing the emperor and establishing Prince Duan Zaiyi's son Pujun as heir to Muzong; fearing foreign obstruction, she followed Rong Lu's advice and changed the designation to "Eldest Imperial Son."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager then considered deposing Guangxu and naming Prince Duan's son Pujun as Tongzhi's heir; fearing foreign interference, she took Rong Lu's counsel and styled the boy the "Eldest Imperial Son" instead.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂作，載漪等稱其術，太后信之，欲倚以排外人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disturbance broke out; Zaiyi and others praised their arts, the Empress Dowager believed them, and wished to rely on them to drive out foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer uprising erupted; Zaiyi and his faction extolled their magic, Cixi believed them, and hoped to use them to expel the foreigners.

sentences.zh: 福祥率甘軍攻使館，月餘不下；

translations.literal: Fuxiang led the Gansu army to attack the legations, and for more than a month could not take them;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fuxiang led the Gansu troops against the legation quarter, yet after more than a month still could not overrun it;

sentences.zh: 榮祿不能阻，載漪等益橫，京師大亂，駢戮忠諫大臣。

translations.literal: Rong Lu could not stop them; Zaiyi and others grew ever more overbearing, the capital fell into great disorder, and loyal remonstrating ministers were executed in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu could not restrain them; Zaiyi's faction grew bolder, the capital descended into chaos, and outspoken loyal ministers were put to death in batches.

sentences.zh: 榮祿踉蹌入言，太后厲色斥之。

translations.literal: Rong Lu staggered in to remonstrate, and the Empress Dowager sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong Lu stumbled in to plead with her, the Empress Dowager rebuked him harshly.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入京，兩宮西幸，駐蹕太原。

translations.literal: The allied armies entered the capital; the two palaces fled west and halted at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied forces entered Beijing, the court fled west and made its stand at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 榮祿請赴行在，不許，命為留京辦事大臣。

translations.literal: Rong Lu requested to go to the traveling palace but was not permitted; he was ordered to serve as minister remaining in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu asked to join the fleeing court but was refused and left behind as minister in charge of affairs in the capital.

sentences.zh: 已而詔詣西安，既至，寵禮有加，賞黃馬褂，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: Soon an edict summoned him to Xi'an; when he arrived, favor and ceremony were increased, he was granted the yellow riding jacket, and bestowed double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to Xi'an, where he was received with exceptional honor, granted the yellow jacket, and given double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.

sentences.zh: 隨扈還京，加太子太保，轉文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: He accompanied the court back to the capital, was given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to grand secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted the court home, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to grand secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十九年卒，贈太傅，諡文忠，晉一等男爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Tutor, given the posthumous title Wenzhong, and advanced to first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year of the reign and was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wenzhong, advanced to first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 榮祿久直內廷，得太后信仗。

translations.literal: Rong Lu long served directly in the inner court and gained the Empress Dowager's trust and reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu had long served inside the palace and enjoyed the Empress Dowager's full trust.

sentences.zh: 眷顧之隆，一時無比。

translations.literal: The grandeur of imperial favor toward him was unmatched in his day.
translations.idiomatic: No one of his time was favored more highly.

sentences.zh: 事無鉅細，常待一言決焉。

translations.literal: Whether matters were great or small, they often awaited a single word from him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small affairs alike often hung on his word alone.

sentences.zh: 王文韶，字夔石，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenshao, style name Kuishi, was a native of Renhe, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshao, styled Kuishi, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，銓戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign he passed the metropolitan examination and was selected as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Xianfeng and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，出為湖北安襄鄖荊道。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, then went out as circuit intendant of An-Xiang-Yun-Jing in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted through the ranks to director, he then served as circuit intendant of An-Xiang-Yun-Jing in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠、李鴻章皆薦其才。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang both recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial judge and transferred to financial commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to provincial judge and then became financial commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of the Tongzhi reign he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he served as acting governor of the province.

sentences.zh: 黔苗亂熾，桂東淪寇域。

translations.literal: The Miao rebellion in Guizhou blazed fiercely, and eastern Guangxi fell into rebel territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao rebellion in Guizhou raged out of control, and eastern Guangxi was overrun by insurgents.

sentences.zh: 文韶條上援黔、防境機宜，以兵事屬按察使席寶田，督其部將蘇元春、龔繼昌等進剿，斬首逆張秀眉烏鴉坡，黔境平。

translations.literal: Wenshao submitted in detail plans for aiding Guizhou and defending the border; he entrusted military affairs to Provincial Judge Xi Baotian, supervised his subordinate generals Su Yuanchun, Gong Jichang, and others in advance and suppression, beheaded the chief rebel Zhang Xiumei at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao laid out a strategy for aiding Guizhou and securing the frontier, placed military operations under Provincial Judge Xi Baotian, and directed generals Su Yuanchun and Gong Jichang in the campaign that killed the rebel leader Zhang Xiumei at Wuyapo and pacified Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 文韶繪苗疆要塞圖，上之朝。

translations.literal: Wenshao drew a map of Miao frontier strongholds and presented it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew a map of Miao frontier fortifications and sent it to the court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，除真。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he received permanent appointment as governor.

sentences.zh: 寧遠莠民倡亂，耒陽硃鴻英复妄稱明裔構眾，先後檄道員陳寶箴討平之。

translations.literal: Wicked commoners in Ningyuan stirred rebellion; Zhu Hongying in Leiyang again falsely claimed Ming descent and gathered a mob; Wenshao successively ordered Circuit Intendant Chen Baozhen to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When troublemakers in Ningyuan rose in revolt and Zhu Hongying in Leiyang falsely claimed Ming descent to rally a mob, Wenshao dispatched Circuit Intendant Chen Baozhen to crush both outbreaks in turn.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，遣總兵謝晉鈞平新化、衡、永土寇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he sent Regional Commander Xie Jinjun to pacify native bandits in Xinhua, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he sent Regional Commander Xie Jinjun to suppress native bandits in Xinhua, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 撫湘六年，內治稱靜謐焉。

translations.literal: During six years governing Hunan, internal administration was said to be tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Over six years as governor of Hunan, his civil administration won a reputation for calm order.

sentences.zh: 入權兵部侍郎，直軍機。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to serve concurrently as vice minister of the Ministry of War and on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve concurrently as vice minister of War and as a Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，各省籥災，中旨罪己。

translations.literal: When drought occurred that year, every province reported disaster, and an imperial rescript pronounced self-reproach.
translations.idiomatic: That year drought struck and provinces across the empire reported famine; the throne issued an edict of self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 文韶亦自陳無狀，詔革職留任。

translations.literal: Wenshao also confessed his unworthiness, and an edict stripped his rank but retained him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao confessed his own failings and was stripped of rank but kept in post.

sentences.zh: 旋除禮部侍郎，兼總理衙門行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and concurrently served in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of Rites and given a concurrent post in the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 八年，御史洪良品、鄧承修劾雲南軍需案，文韶坐失察，奪二級。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Censors Hong Liangpin and Deng Chengxiu impeached the Yunnan military supplies case; Wenshao was punished for failure of supervision and stripped of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Censors Hong Liangpin and Deng Chengxiu exposed corruption in Yunnan military supplies; Wenshao was held negligent and demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 乞養歸，終母喪，還前除。

translations.literal: He requested leave to care for his parents and returned home, completed mourning for his mother, and was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to nurse his parents, returned home, completed mourning for his mother, and was then restored to office.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 武定會匪陷富民、祿勸，人心恟懼。

translations.literal: The Wuding secret-society rebels seized Fumin and Luquan, and popular hearts were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Secret-society rebels in Wuding seized Fumin and Luquan, throwing the populace into panic.

sentences.zh: 文韶斬獲叛將，三日而定。

translations.literal: Wenshao beheaded and captured the rebel generals, and within three days it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao captured and executed the rebel leaders, and order was restored within three days.

sentences.zh: 無何，鎮邊夷亂起，檄迤南道劉春霖分道進攻，拓地三百里。

translations.literal: Before long a frontier Yi rebellion broke out; he ordered Circuit Intendant Liu Chunlin of Yinan to attack by separate routes and expanded territory by three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a Yi uprising on the frontier erupted; he ordered Liu Chunlin, circuit intendant of southern Yunnan, to advance on several fronts and extended control over three hundred li of territory.

sentences.zh: 徙建廳城於猛朗，募勇屯墾。

translations.literal: He moved and rebuilt the subprefectural seat at Menglang and recruited braves for garrison farming.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the subprefectural seat to Menglang and recruited militia for garrison colonization.

sentences.zh: 改臨安猛丁歸流，移府經歷駐其地。

translations.literal: He changed Mengding in Lin'an to direct administration and moved the prefectural assistant magistrate to be stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: He placed Mengding in Lin'an under regular civil administration and stationed a prefectural assistant magistrate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 其餘寇亂及土族叛服不常，皆隨時殄滅。

translations.literal: Other bandit disturbances and tribal groups whose loyalty and submission were inconstant were all exterminated as occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Other outbreaks and restive native groups were suppressed whenever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 初，英、法並緬、越後，西南緣邊防務益棘。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Britain and France had annexed Burma and Vietnam, frontier defense along the southwest border grew ever more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: After Britain and France had absorbed Burma and Vietnam, defense along the southwestern frontier became increasingly precarious.

sentences.zh: 文韶綏靖各路土司，令自為守。

translations.literal: Wenshao pacified the various native chieftains along the routes and ordered them to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao pacified the native chieftains and ordered them to hold their own territories.

sentences.zh: 會日韓啟釁，詔入都詢方略。

translations.literal: When Japan and Korea provoked hostilities, an edict summoned him to the capital to consult on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between Japan and Korea, he was summoned to the capital for strategic consultation.

sentences.zh: 既至，奉幫辦北洋之命。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he received orders to assist in managing Beiyang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was ordered to assist in Beiyang affairs.

sentences.zh: 鴻章赴日議和，文韶權直隸總督、北洋大臣。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang went to Japan to negotiate peace, Wenshao acted as governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang minister.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Hongzhang went to Japan to negotiate peace, Wenshao served as acting governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang minister.

sentences.zh: 和議成，實授。

translations.literal: After peace was concluded, he received regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was concluded, he received the posts in full.

sentences.zh: 時關內外主客軍四百餘營，酌留湘、淮、豫三十營，餘悉散遣，士卒帖然。

translations.literal: At that time within and beyond the passes there were more than four hundred camps of regular and guest armies; he considered retaining thirty camps from Hunan, Huai, and Henan armies, dispersed all the rest, and the soldiers submitted peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred regular and auxiliary camps then garrisoned north China; he kept thirty Hunan, Huai, and Henan battalions and disbanded the rest without unrest among the troops.

sentences.zh: 建議籌修旅大砲台，謂：「旅順舊台密於防前，疏於防後，敵自大連灣入，遂失所芘；

translations.literal: He proposed planning repairs to the Lüda fort batteries, stating: "The old batteries at Lüshun were dense in defense of the front and sparse in defense of the rear; when the enemy entered from Dalian Bay, protection was lost;
translations.idiomatic: He urged rebuilding the fortifications at Lüshun and Dalian, arguing: "The old batteries at Lüshun were strong facing the sea but weak to the rear; when the enemy came in through Dalian Bay, the position was lost;

sentences.zh: 大連舊台，專顧防海，未及防陸，敵自金州登岸，遂不能支。

translations.literal: the old batteries at Dalian looked only to defense at sea and did not reach to land defense; the enemy landed from Jinzhou and thus could not be held."
translations.idiomatic: the old Dalian batteries guarded only the seaward approach and not the land side; once the enemy landed at Jinzhou, the line could not be held."

sentences.zh: 今重整海防，必彌其罅隙。

translations.literal: Now in reorganizing coastal defense, the gaps must be closed.
translations.idiomatic: In rebuilding coastal defenses, those gaps must be closed."

sentences.zh: 」又請加意水師、武備各學堂，以儲將才，嫺武幹，俟財力稍足，徐圖擴充。

translations.literal: He also requested greater attention to the naval and military academies to store up command talent and train military ability, and when finances were somewhat sufficient, gradually to plan expansion.
translations.idiomatic: He also called for greater support for the naval and military academies to train officers and develop martial skill, with gradual expansion once finances allowed.

sentences.zh: 又陳河運漕糧積弊，請蘇漕統歸海運，他若勘吉林三姓金礦、磁州煤礦，踵鴻章後次第成之，而京漢鐵路亦興築於是時矣。

translations.literal: He also stated the accumulated abuses of grain transport by the Grand Canal and requested that Jiangsu tribute grain be wholly shifted to sea transport; other projects such as surveying the gold mines of the Three Surnames in Jilin and the coal mines of Cizhou were completed in succession following Hongzhang's lead, and the Beijing-Hankou Railway was also begun at this time.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed longstanding abuses in canal grain transport and urged shifting Jiangsu tribute entirely to sea routes; surveys of Jilin's Three Surnames gold mines and Cizhou's coal mines followed Li Hongzhang's initiatives, and construction of the Beijing-Hankou Railway also began in this period.

sentences.zh: 又奏設北洋大學堂、鐵路學堂、育才館、俄文館，造就甚眾。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to establish Beiyang University, the Railway Academy, the Yucai Hall, and the Russian Language School, training very many students.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded Beiyang University, a railway school, the Yucai Hall, and a Russian language institute, turning out a great many graduates.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入贊軍機，以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he entered to assist on the Grand Council, serving as minister of the Ministry of Revenue and associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he joined the Grand Council as minister of Revenue and associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪仇教，文韶力言外釁不可啟，不見納。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxers hated Christianity; Wenshao strongly urged that foreign conflict must not be provoked, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, as the Boxers turned against Christianity, Wenshao warned repeatedly against provoking foreign powers, but his counsel was ignored.

sentences.zh: 宮車既出，三日，始追及懷來。

translations.literal: After the imperial carriage had departed, only after three days did he catch up at Huailai.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already fled when he caught up at Huailai three days later.

sentences.zh: 自聯軍犯京，事急，兩宮召軍機，惟文韶一人入見，諭必侍行。

translations.literal: From the time the allied armies threatened the capital, when matters were urgent the two palaces summoned the Grand Council, and only Wenshao alone was admitted to audience and instructed that he must attend on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies threatened Beijing, the court summoned the Grand Council, but only Wenshao was admitted and told he must accompany the flight.

sentences.zh: 至是立召對，泣慰之，遂隨扈，自晉入秦，晉體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: At this he was immediately summoned to special audience; they wept and comforted him, and he then followed in attendance; from Shanxi they entered Shaanxi, and he was promoted to grand secretary of the Tiren Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned at once to a private audience, the empresses wept as they comforted him, and he joined the flight west from Shanxi into Shaanxi, receiving promotion to grand secretary of the Tiren Hall.

sentences.zh: 明年，改外務部會辦大臣，旋賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to co-minister of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and soon granted the yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became co-minister of Foreign Affairs and was soon granted the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 署全權大臣，命先還京，佐辦中俄條約。

translations.literal: He served as acting plenipotentiary minister and was ordered to return to the capital first to assist in the Sino-Russian treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Made acting plenipotentiary, he was sent back to the capital ahead of the court to help negotiate the Sino-Russian treaty.

sentences.zh: 交還東三省及關外鐵路，事寧，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: After the return of the Three Eastern Provinces and the railways beyond the passes and the settlement of affairs, he was granted double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Once Manchuria and the railways beyond the passes had been restored and affairs settled, he was awarded double-eyed peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 充政務處大臣，督辦路礦總局。

translations.literal: He served as minister of the Bureau of Government Affairs and supervised the Bureau General of Railways and Mines.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Bureau of Government Affairs and supervised the Bureau General of Railways and Mines.

sentences.zh: 轉文淵閣，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion and promoted to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the Wenyuan Pavilion to grand secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，免直軍機。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was relieved of direct service on the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he left the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 明年，稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: The next year he pleaded illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he cited illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 文韶歷官中外，詳練吏職，究識大體，然更事久，明於趨避，亦往往被口語。

translations.literal: Wenshao served in office both within and outside the capital, was thoroughly versed in official duties and understood the larger pattern, yet having long experience in affairs he was clear about avoiding danger and was also often subject to gossip.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao served at court and in the provinces, knew administration inside out, and grasped the larger picture—yet long experience had taught him how to sidestep trouble, and he was often criticized for it.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，鄉舉重逢，賜太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he again encountered the anniversary of passing the provincial examination and was granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, on the anniversary of his provincial examination success, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其冬，卒，年七十九，晉贈太保，諡文勤。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged seventy-nine; he was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter at seventy-nine, posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 張之洞，字香濤，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong, style name Xiangtao, was a native of Nanpi, Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong, styled Xiangtao, came from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 少有大略，務博覽為詞章，記誦絕人。

translations.literal: In youth he had great strategic vision, devoted himself to wide reading and literary composition, and his memory was unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed broad vision, read voraciously, wrote with facility, and possessed a memory few could match.

sentences.zh: 年十六，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he took first place in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，成進士，廷對策不循常式，用一甲三名授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination; in the palace examination his policy essay did not follow the usual form, yet he was placed among the top three of the first class and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Tongzhi; his palace examination essay broke convention, yet he still ranked third in the first class and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 六年，充浙江鄉試副考官，旋督湖北學政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as associate examiner for the Zhejiang provincial examination, then was appointed educational commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as associate examiner for Zhejiang's provincial exams, then became educational commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十二年，典試四川，就授學政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he presided over the Sichuan examination and was thereupon appointed educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he presided over the Sichuan examinations and was appointed educational commissioner on the spot.

sentences.zh: 所取士多俊才，遊其門者，皆私自喜得為學塗徑。

translations.literal: Those he selected were mostly outstanding talents; those who studied under him all privately rejoiced at having found a path in learning.
translations.idiomatic: The scholars he chose were mostly brilliant men, and those who studied under him felt they had found a true mentor on the scholarly path.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，擢司業，再遷洗馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was promoted to vice director of studies and again transferred to groom of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign he rose to vice director of studies and then to groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 之洞以文儒致清要，遇事敢為大言。

translations.literal: Zhidong, as a literary scholar, attained a pure and exalted post, and when matters arose he dared to speak in grand terms.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar-official who had risen to a prestigious post, Zhidong was known for bold pronouncements whenever controversy arose.

sentences.zh: 俄人議歸伊犁，與使俄大臣崇厚訂新約十八條。

translations.literal: When the Russians negotiated the return of Ili, Minister to Russia Chonghou concluded a new treaty of eighteen articles with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Russia agreed to return Ili, Minister to Russia Chonghou signed a new eighteen-article treaty with Moscow.

sentences.zh: 之洞論奏其失，請斬崇厚，毀俄約。

translations.literal: Zhidong memorialized analyzing its errors, requesting that Chonghou be beheaded and the Russian treaty annulled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong memorialized detailing its flaws, demanding Chonghou's execution and the abrogation of the Russian treaty.

sentences.zh: 疏上，乃褫崇厚職治罪，以侍郎曾紀澤為使俄大臣，議改約。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Chonghou was stripped of office and punished, and Vice Minister Zeng Jize was appointed minister to Russia to negotiate revision of the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial reached the throne, Chonghou was dismissed and punished, and Vice Minister Zeng Jize was sent to Russia to renegotiate the treaty.

sentences.zh: 六年，授侍講，再遷庶子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed expositor, then again promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became an expositor and was soon promoted to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 复論紀澤定約執成見，但論界務，不爭商務，並附陳設防、練兵之策。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that Jize, in concluding the treaty, clung to fixed views, discussing only boundary affairs and not contesting commercial matters, and appended proposals for frontier defense and military training.
translations.idiomatic: He again criticized Jize for clinging to preconceptions—settling boundaries but not commercial rights—and appended proposals for frontier defense and troop training.

sentences.zh: 疏凡七八上。

translations.literal: His memorials altogether numbered seven or eight.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted seven or eight such memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 往者詞臣率雍容養望，自之洞喜言事，同時寶廷、陳寶琛、張佩綸輩崛起，糾彈時政，號為清流。

translations.literal: Formerly literary officials generally cultivated reputation with easy grace; since Zhidong delighted in speaking on affairs, at the same time Baoting, Chen Baochen, Zhang Peilun, and others rose up, impeaching current policy, and were called the Pure Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin officials had long cultivated reputations in comfortable silence; but once Zhidong took to remonstrance, contemporaries such as Baoting, Chen Baochen, and Zhang Peilun rose to impeach current policy and were known as the Pure Stream faction.

sentences.zh: 七年，由侍講學士擢閣學。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted from expositor of the Hanlin Academy to academy bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he rose from expositor of the Hanlin Academy to academy bachelor.

sentences.zh: 俄授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 當大祲後，首劾布政使葆亨、冀寧道王定安等黷貨，舉廉明吏五人，條上治晉要務，未及行，移督兩廣。

translations.literal: After the great famine he first impeached Financial Commissioner Baoheng, Jining Circuit Intendant Wang Ding'an, and others for corruption, recommended five incorrupt officials, and submitted in detail the essentials for governing Shanxi; before these could be carried out, he was transferred to supervise the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After the great famine he impeached Financial Commissioner Baoheng, Jining Circuit Intendant Wang Ding'an, and others for corruption, recommended five upright officials, and laid out priorities for governing Shanxi—but before his reforms could take effect, he was transferred to the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 八年，法越事起，建議當速遣師赴援，示以戰意，乃可居間調解。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; he proposed that troops should quickly be dispatched to aid, showing a will to fight, and only then could one mediate between the parties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Franco-Vietnamese conflict erupted, he urged rapid dispatch of troops to show a willingness to fight—only then, he argued, could China mediate effectively.

sentences.zh: 因薦唐炯、徐延旭、張曜材任將帥。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Tang Jiong, Xu Yanxu, and Zhang Yao as men whose talent fitted them for command.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Tang Jiong, Xu Yanxu, and Zhang Yao as capable commanders.

sentences.zh: 十年春，入覲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he entered the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year he went to the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 四月，兩廣總督張樹聲解任專治軍，遂以之洞代。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Governor-General Zhang Shusheng of the two Guang provinces was relieved to devote himself solely to military affairs, and Zhidong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Governor-General Zhang Shusheng was relieved of civil duties to focus on the war effort, and Zhidong took his place.

sentences.zh: 當是時，雲貴總督岑毓英、廣西巡撫潘鼎新皆出督師，尚書彭玉麟治兵廣東。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General Cen Yuying of Yunnan and Guizhou and Governor Pan Dingxin of Guangxi both went out to command armies, and Minister Peng Yulin directed troops in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor-General Cen Yuying of Yunnan-Guizhou and Governor Pan Dingxin of Guangxi were both in the field, while Minister Peng Yulin directed forces in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 越將劉永福者，故中國人，素驍勇，與法抗。

translations.literal: The Vietnamese general Liu Yongfu was formerly a Chinese subject, naturally fierce and brave, and resisted the French.
translations.idiomatic: The Vietnamese commander Liu Yongfu was a Chinese by origin, renowned for valor, and fought the French.

sentences.zh: 法攻越未能下，復分兵攻台灣，其後遂據基隆。

translations.literal: The French attacked Vietnam but could not subdue it; they again divided forces to attack Taiwan, and afterward seized Keelung.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to conquer Vietnam, the French diverted forces to Taiwan and eventually seized Keelung.

sentences.zh: 朝議和戰久不決，之洞至，言戰事氣自倍，以玉麟夙著威望，虛己聽從之。

translations.literal: Court debate on war or peace long remained unsettled; when Zhidong arrived, talk of war doubled in spirit, and because Yulin had long enjoyed great prestige, he humbled himself and followed Yulin's lead.
translations.idiomatic: With the court deadlocked over war or peace, Zhidong's arrival doubled fighting spirit; deferring to the long-respected Peng Yulin, he followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 奏請主事唐景崧募健卒出關，與永福相犄角。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting Secretary Tang Jingsong to recruit stalwart soldiers and go beyond the pass, supporting Yongfu in mutual flanking.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that Secretary Tang Jingsong recruit tough fighters to cross the border and coordinate with Yongfu in a pincer movement.

sentences.zh: 朝旨因就加永福提督、景崧五品卿銜，炯、延旭亦皆已至巡撫，當前敵，被劾得罪去，並坐舉者。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript thereupon promoted Yongfu to provincial commander and granted Jingsong fifth-rank noble rank; Jiong and Yanxu, who had already reached the rank of governor and faced the enemy, were impeached, punished, and dismissed, and those who had recommended them were implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: The court promoted Yongfu to provincial commander and gave Jingsong fifth-rank noble rank; but Tang Jiong and Xu Yanxu, already governors on the front lines, were impeached, dismissed, and their recommenders punished along with them.

sentences.zh: 之洞獨以籌餉械勞，免議。

translations.literal: Zhidong alone, on account of his labor in raising funds and ordnance, was exempted from censure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong alone escaped censure, credited with the hard work of raising funds and supplies.

sentences.zh: 廣西軍既敗於越，朝旨免鼎新，以提督蘇元春統其軍，而之洞復奏遣提督馮子材、總兵王孝祺等，皆宿將，於是滇、越兩軍合扼鎮南關，殊死戰，遂克諒山。

translations.literal: After the Guangxi army was defeated in Vietnam, an imperial rescript dismissed Dingxin and placed Provincial Commander Su Yuanchun in command of his forces; Zhidong again memorialized to dispatch Provincial Commander Feng Zicai, Regional Commander Wang Xiaoqi, and others, all veteran generals; thereupon the Yunnan and Vietnam armies united to hold Zhennanguan, fought a desperate battle, and thus captured Lang Son.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangxi army's defeat in Vietnam, Pan Dingxin was dismissed and Su Yuanchun took command; Zhidong then sent veteran generals Feng Zicai and Wang Xiaoqi, and the Yunnan and Vietnamese forces united at Zhennanguan, fought a desperate battle, and captured Lang Son.

sentences.zh: 會法提督孤拔攻閩、浙，砲毀其坐船，孤拔殪，而我軍不知，法原停戰，廷議許焉。

translations.literal: At the same time French Admiral Courbet attacked Fujian and Zhejiang; cannon destroyed his flagship, Courbet perished, but our army did not know; France had originally proposed a ceasefire, and court deliberation approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile French Admiral Courbet attacked Fujian and Zhejiang; cannon fire sank his flagship and killed him—but our forces did not know. France had already sought a ceasefire, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 授李鴻章全權大臣，定約，以北圻為界。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang was appointed plenipotentiary minister to conclude the treaty, setting the northern part of Tonkin as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang was made plenipotentiary and signed a treaty setting the northern part of Tonkin as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 敘克諒山功，賞花翎。

translations.literal: In recounting the merit of capturing Lang Son, he was granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: For the capture of Lang Son he was awarded peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 之洞恥言和，則陰自圖強，設廣東水陸師學堂，創槍砲廠，開礦務局。

translations.literal: Zhidong was ashamed to speak of peace, and therefore secretly planned self-strengthening: he established the Guangdong Naval and Military Academy, founded an arsenal, and opened a mining bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of the peace settlement, Zhidong quietly pursued self-strengthening: he founded the Guangdong Naval and Military Academy, an arsenal, and a mining bureau.

sentences.zh: 疏請大治水師，歲提專款購兵艦。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting major development of the navy, with an annual special fund to purchase warships.
translations.idiomatic: He urged major naval expansion, with an annual dedicated fund to purchase warships.

sentences.zh: 復立廣雅書院。

translations.literal: He also established the Guangya Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded the Guangya Academy.

sentences.zh: 武備文事並舉。

translations.literal: Military preparedness and literary affairs were pursued together.
translations.idiomatic: Military training and scholarly education advanced side by side.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he concurrently served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he also served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 於兩粵邊防控制之宜，輒多更置。

translations.literal: Regarding what was fitting for controlling the frontier defenses of the two Yue regions, he often made many changes in deployment.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently reorganized frontier defenses across the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 著沿海險要圖說上之。

translations.literal: He composed an illustrated account of coastal strategic points and presented it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled an illustrated survey of coastal defenses and sent it to the court.

sentences.zh: 在粵六年，調補兩湖。

translations.literal: After six years in Guangdong he was transferred to fill the two Hu posts.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in Guangdong he was transferred to the two Hu provinces.

sentences.zh: 會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦。

translations.literal: When the Naval Office memorialized requesting construction of the Beijing-Tongzhou Railway, censors and remonstrating officials contended over the harm of railways and requested that work be halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Naval Office proposed building the Beijing-Tongzhou Railway, censors protested the dangers of railways and demanded a halt.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢等請試修邊地，便用兵；

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe and others requested trial construction in frontier regions to facilitate troop movement;
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe and others proposed trial lines in frontier regions to ease troop movements;

sentences.zh: 徐會灃請改修德州濟寧路，利漕運。

translations.literal: Xu Huifeng requested instead construction of the Dezhou-Jining route to benefit grain transport by the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huifeng urged building the Dezhou-Jining line instead to aid canal grain transport.

sentences.zh: 之洞議曰：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之。

translations.literal: Zhidong deliberated, saying: "The benefit of building railways lies greatest in circulating native goods and enriching the people's livelihood; moving troops and transporting provisions come next.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong argued: "The greatest benefit of railways is moving local goods and enriching people's livelihoods; troop movement and supply transport come second.

sentences.zh: 今宜自京外盧溝橋起，經河南以達湖北漢口鎮。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to begin outside the capital at Lugou Bridge, pass through Henan, and reach Hankou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The line should run from Lugou Bridge outside Beijing through Henan to Hankou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 此幹路樞紐，中國大利所萃也。

translations.literal: This trunk line is the pivot; China's great benefits converge upon it.
translations.idiomatic: This trunk line would be the pivot where China's greatest advantages would converge.

sentences.zh: 河北路成，則三晉之轍接於井陘，關隴之驂交於洛口；

translations.literal: When the Hebei section is completed, the wheel tracks of the Three Jins will connect at Jingxing, and the paired horses of Guanlong will meet at Luokou;
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hebei section was built, Shanxi's roads would link at Jingxing and Shaanxi-Gansu's routes would meet at Luokou;

sentences.zh: 自河以南，則東引淮、吳，南通湘、蜀，萬里聲息，刻期可通。

translations.literal: south of the river it would draw east to Huai and Wu, connect south to Xiang and Shu, and news from ten thousand li could be communicated within a set period.
translations.idiomatic: south of the river it would reach east to the Huai and Wu regions and south to Hunan and Sichuan, so that news from thousands of miles could travel on schedule.

sentences.zh: 其便利有數端：內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；

translations.literal: Its conveniences have several points: lying inland in the interior, there is no worry of drawing in the enemy—benefit one;
translations.idiomatic: He listed seven advantages: running through the interior, it would not invite enemy invasion—first;

sentences.zh: 原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二；

translations.literal: the open wilderness is vast, graves and cottages are easily avoided—benefit two;
translations.idiomatic: the open countryside would make graves and dwellings easy to avoid—second;

sentences.zh: 廠盛站多，役夫賈客可舍舊圖新，利三；

translations.literal: with many flourishing stations, laborers and merchants can abandon old ways for new—benefit three;
translations.idiomatic: numerous stations would let laborers and merchants shift to new livelihoods—third;

sentences.zh: 以一路控八九省之衢，人貨輻輳，足裕餉源，利四；

translations.literal: with one route controlling the thoroughfares of eight or nine provinces, people and goods will converge, sufficient to enrich sources of revenue—benefit four;
translations.idiomatic: one line would command the routes of eight or nine provinces, concentrating people and goods to enrich revenue—fourth;

sentences.zh: 近畿有事，淮、楚精兵崇朝可集，利五；

translations.literal: if trouble arises near the capital, elite troops of Huai and Chu can be assembled within a morning—benefit five;
translations.idiomatic: if trouble struck near the capital, Huai and Chu elite troops could assemble within a day—fifth;

sentences.zh: 太原旺煤鐵，運行便則開採必多，利六；

translations.literal: Taiyuan abounds in coal and iron; if transport is convenient, mining will surely increase—benefit six;
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan's rich coal and iron would be mined more heavily once transport improved—sixth;

sentences.zh: 海上用兵，漕運無梗，利七。

translations.literal: if war occurs at sea, grain transport by the Grand Canal will be unimpeded—benefit seven.
translations.idiomatic: in wartime at sea, canal grain transport would remain unblocked—seventh.

sentences.zh: 有此七利，分段分年成之。

translations.literal: With these seven benefits, it should be completed section by section and year by year.
translations.idiomatic: With these seven advantages, he urged building the line in sections over successive years.

sentences.zh: 北路責之直隸總督，南路責之湖廣總督，副以河南巡撫。

translations.literal: The northern section would be charged to the governor-general of Zhili, the southern section to the governor-general of Huguang, assisted by the governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The northern section would fall to the governor-general of Zhili, the southern to the governor-general of Huguang, with the governor of Henan assisting.

sentences.zh: 」得旨報可，遂有移楚之命。

translations.literal: An imperial rescript approved the report, and thereupon came the order transferring him to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved, and he received orders to transfer to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 大冶產鐵，江西萍鄉產煤，之洞乃奏開鍊鐵廠漢陽大別山下，資路用，兼設槍砲鋼藥專廠。

translations.literal: Daye produced iron and Pingxiang in Jiangxi produced coal; Zhidong then memorialized to open an ironworks below Dabie Mountain at Hanyang to supply the railway, and concurrently established specialized factories for firearms, cannon, steel, and powder.
translations.idiomatic: With iron from Daye and coal from Pingxiang in Jiangxi, Zhidong opened an ironworks at the foot of Dabie Mountain in Hanyang for the railway, plus specialized factories for firearms, cannon, steel, and powder.

sentences.zh: 又以荊襄宜桑棉麻枲而饒皮革，設織布、紡紗、繅絲、制麻革諸局，佐之以堤工，通之以幣政。

translations.literal: Because Jing-Xiang was suited to mulberry, cotton, hemp, and ramie and abounded in leather, he established bureaus for weaving cloth, spinning yarn, reeling silk, and making hemp and leather goods, supplemented by dike works and connected by currency policy.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing-Xiang region's mulberry, cotton, hemp, ramie, and leather resources led him to establish weaving, spinning, silk-reeling, and leather workshops, supplemented by dike projects and currency reforms.

sentences.zh: 由是湖北財賦稱饒，土木工作亦日興矣。

translations.literal: From this Hubei's revenues were said to be abundant, and construction work also grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei's revenues grew abundant and construction flourished day by day.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，中東事棘，代劉坤一督兩江，至則巡閱江防，購新出後膛砲，改築西式砲台，設專將專兵領之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Sino-Japanese affair grew critical; he replaced Liu Kunyi as governor-general of the two Jiang regions; upon arrival he inspected river defenses, purchased newly produced breech-loading cannon, rebuilt batteries in Western style, and appointed dedicated generals and dedicated troops to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, as the Sino-Japanese crisis deepened, he replaced Liu Kunyi as governor-general of the two Jiang regions; on arrival he inspected river defenses, bought new breech-loading guns, rebuilt batteries in Western style, and assigned dedicated commanders and troops.

sentences.zh: 募德人教練，名曰「江南自強軍」。

translations.literal: He recruited Germans as instructors, naming the force the "Jiangnan Self-Strengthening Army."
translations.idiomatic: He hired German instructors for a force called the "Jiangnan Self-Strengthening Army."

sentences.zh: 採東西規制，廣立武備、農工商、鐵路、方言、軍醫諸學堂。

translations.literal: Adopting Eastern and Western regulations, he broadly established academies for military affairs, agriculture, industry, commerce, railways, foreign languages, and military medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting Eastern and Western models, he founded schools for military affairs, agriculture, industry, commerce, railways, foreign languages, and military medicine.

sentences.zh: 尋還任湖北。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his post in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his post in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 時國威新挫，朝士日議變法，廢時文，改試策論。

translations.literal: At that time national prestige had been newly humbled; court officials daily debated reform, abolishing the eight-legged essay and changing examinations to policy discourse.
translations.idiomatic: National prestige freshly humbled, court officials debated reform daily—abolishing the eight-legged essay and switching examinations to policy essays.

sentences.zh: 之洞言：「廢時文，非廢五經、四書也，故文體必正，命題之意必嚴。

translations.literal: Zhidong said: "Abolishing the timed essay does not mean abolishing the Five Classics and Four Books; therefore the literary form must be correct and the intent of the examination topics must be strict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong argued: "Abolishing the eight-legged essay does not mean abandoning the Five Classics and Four Books; the essay form must remain proper and examination topics must be rigorous.

sentences.zh: 否則國家重教之旨不顯，必致不讀經文，背道忘本，非細故也。

translations.literal: Otherwise the state's purpose in honoring education will not be manifest, and it will inevitably lead to not reading the classics, turning one's back on the Way and forgetting one's roots—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the state's educational purpose would be lost, scholars would stop reading the classics, abandon the Way and forget their roots—a matter of grave consequence.

sentences.zh: 今宜首場試史論及本朝政法，二場試時務，三場以經義終焉。

translations.literal: Now the first session should test historical discourse and current-dynasty politics and law, the second session current affairs, and the third session should conclude with classical interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: The first session should test historical essays and current-dynasty law; the second, current affairs; the third, classical interpretation.

sentences.zh: 各隨場去留而層遞取之，庶少流弊。

translations.literal: Candidates should pass or fail at each session and be selected by successive stages, so that abuses may be somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates should pass or fail at each stage, advancing layer by layer, to reduce abuses.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「武科宜罷騎射、刀石，專試火器。

translations.literal: He also said: "The military examination should abolish mounted archery and stone-throwing with blades, and test firearms exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged abolishing mounted archery and blade-throwing in military examinations and testing firearms exclusively.

sentences.zh: 欲挽重文輕武之習，必使兵皆識字，勵行伍以科舉。

translations.literal: Wishing to reverse the custom of honoring literature and slighting the military, soldiers must all be made literate, and men in the ranks encouraged through the civil examination system.
translations.idiomatic: To reverse the habit of valuing scholars over soldiers, troops must learn to read and military men should be encouraged through the examination system.

sentences.zh: 」二十四年，政變作，之洞先著勸學篇以見意，得免議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the political coup occurred; Zhidong had earlier written Exhortation to Learning to express his views and thereby escaped censure.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when the coup struck, Zhidong had already published Exhortation to Learning to signal his position and thus escaped blame.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京師拳亂，時坤一督兩江，鴻章督兩廣，袁世凱撫山東，要請之洞，同與外國領事定保護東南之約。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disturbance broke out in the capital; at that time Kunyi governed the two Jiang regions, Hongzhang the two Guang provinces, and Yuan Shikai governed Shandong; they urgently requested Zhidong to join with foreign consuls in fixing an agreement to protect the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, as the Boxer uprising engulfed Beijing, Kunyi governed the two Jiang regions, Hongzhang the two Guang provinces, and Yuan Shikai Shandong; they urgently enlisted Zhidong to join foreign consuls in a pact to protect the southeast.

sentences.zh: 及聯軍內犯，兩宮西幸，而東南幸無事。

translations.literal: When the allied armies invaded inland, the two palaces fled west, while the southeast fortunately remained undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies invaded, the court fled west while the southeast remained untouched.

sentences.zh: 明年，和議成，兩宮回鑾。

translations.literal: The next year peace was concluded and the two palaces returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year peace was settled and the court returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In recounting merit he was given the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以兵事粗定，乃與坤一合上變法三疏。

translations.literal: As military affairs were roughly settled, he joined Kunyi in submitting three memorials on reform.
translations.idiomatic: Once military affairs had roughly settled, he and Kunyi jointly submitted three reform memorials.

sentences.zh: 其論中國積弱不振之故，宜變通者十二事，宜採西法者十一事。

translations.literal: They discussed the reasons for China's accumulated weakness and failure to revive: twelve matters that should be changed, and eleven matters in which Western methods should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: They analyzed why China had grown weak, listing twelve areas needing change and eleven Western practices to adopt.

sentences.zh: 於是停捐納，去書吏，考差役，卹刑獄，籌八旗生計，裁屯衛，汰綠營，定礦律、商律、路律、交涉律，行銀圓，取印花稅，擴郵政。

translations.literal: Thereupon purchase of office was halted, clerical runners removed, yamen runners examined, prisons treated with compassion, Eight Banner livelihoods planned, garrison colonies cut, Green Standard troops reduced, mining, commercial, railway, and foreign-relations laws fixed, silver dollars circulated, stamp tax levied, and postal service expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase of office was halted, clerks and runners reformed, prisons humanized, Banner livelihoods addressed, garrison colonies cut, Green Standard troops reduced, mining, commercial, railway, and foreign-relations laws drafted, silver dollars introduced, stamp taxes levied, and postal service expanded.

sentences.zh: 其尤要者，則設學堂，停科舉，獎遊學。

translations.literal: Most important of all were establishing schools, halting the civil examinations, and rewarding study abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Most important were establishing schools, ending the civil examinations, and rewarding study abroad.

sentences.zh: 皆次第行焉。

translations.literal: All were carried out in succession.
translations.idiomatic: These reforms were implemented one after another.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，充督辦商務大臣，再署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he served as supervising minister of commerce and again acted as governor-general of the two Jiang regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he supervised commerce and again served as acting governor-general of the two Jiang regions.

sentences.zh: 有道員私獻商人金二十萬為壽，請開礦海州，立劾罷之。

translations.literal: A circuit intendant privately presented two hundred thousand taels from a merchant as a birthday gift, requesting permission to open mines at Haizhou; Zhidong immediately impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a circuit intendant privately offered him two hundred thousand taels from a merchant as a birthday gift to open mines at Haizhou, Zhidong impeached and dismissed him at once.

sentences.zh: 考鹽法利弊，設兵輪緝私，歲有贏課。

translations.literal: He examined the advantages and disadvantages of the salt monopoly, established armed steamers to suppress smuggling, and each year produced surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the salt monopoly, he deployed armed steamers against smuggling and produced annual surpluses.

sentences.zh: 明年，入覲，充經濟特科閱卷大臣，釐定大學堂章程，畢，仍命還任。

translations.literal: The next year he entered the capital for audience, served as chief examiner for the special economic examination, settled the regulations of the university, and when finished was still ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went to the capital, served as chief examiner for the special economic examination, finalized university regulations, and was then sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 陛辭奏對，請化除滿、漢畛域，以彰聖德，遏亂萌，上為動​​容。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he memorialized and spoke, requesting the elimination of Manchu-Han barriers to manifest sagely virtue and check the sprouting of disorder; the emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he urged breaking down Manchu-Han barriers to display imperial virtue and forestall unrest; the emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 旋裁巡撫，以之洞兼之。

translations.literal: Soon the governorship was abolished and Zhidong was given concurrent charge.
translations.idiomatic: The governorship was soon abolished and Zhidong given concurrent charge.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，晉協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，內召，擢體仁閣大學士，授軍機大臣，兼筦學部。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the capital, promoted to grand secretary of the Tiren Hall, appointed Grand Councilor, and given concurrent charge of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon summoned to the capital, he became grand secretary of the Tiren Hall, Grand Councilor, and head of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，督辦粵漢鐵路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he supervised the Canton-Hankou Railway.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he supervised construction of the Canton-Hankou Railway.

sentences.zh: 德宗暨慈禧皇太后相繼崩，醇親王載灃監國攝政。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession; Prince Chun Zaifeng served as regent and held power as acting ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangxu and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession; Prince Chun Zaifeng became regent.

sentences.zh: 之洞以顧命重臣晉太子太保。

translations.literal: Zhidong, as a heavy minister entrusted at the deathbed, was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As a deathbed-appointed minister, Zhidong was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 逾年，親貴浸用事，通私謁。

translations.literal: After a year the imperial kin gradually took power and accepted private audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year imperial princes gained influence and accepted private audiences.

sentences.zh: 議立海軍，之洞言海軍費絀可緩立，爭之不得。

translations.literal: When a navy was proposed, Zhidong said naval funds were insufficient and establishment could be deferred; he argued but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When a navy was proposed, Zhidong argued funds were insufficient and establishment could wait, but he could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 移疾，遂卒，年七十三，朝野震悼。

translations.literal: He reported illness, then died, aged seventy-three; court and populace were shaken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: He reported illness and died at seventy-three; court and country mourned deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，諡文襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor with the title Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 之洞短身巨髯，風儀峻整。

translations.literal: Zhidong was short in stature with a great beard, his bearing stern and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: Short in stature with a great beard, Zhidong carried himself with stern dignity.

sentences.zh: 蒞官所至，必有興作。

translations.literal: Wherever he took office there were always new undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he launched new projects.

sentences.zh: 務宏大，不問費多寡。

translations.literal: He pursued grandeur and did not inquire how much expense was involved.
translations.idiomatic: He thought big and never counted the cost.

sentences.zh: 愛才好客，名流文士爭趨之。

translations.literal: He loved talent and delighted in guests; eminent literary men all rushed to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talent and entertained generously; leading scholars flocked to his door.

sentences.zh: 任疆寄數十年，及卒，家不增一畝雲。

translations.literal: He held frontier responsibilities for several decades, yet when he died his household had not increased by a single mu of land.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held frontier posts for decades, his family owned not a single additional mu of land when he died.

sentences.zh: 瞿鴻禨，字子玖，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Qu Hongji, style name Zijiu, was a native of Shanhua, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Hongji, styled Zijiu, came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the tenth year of Tongzhi and was made a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，大考一等，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, in the great examination he placed first class and was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he ranked first in the palace examination and was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 久乃遷詹事，晉內閣學士。

translations.literal: Only after a long time was he transferred to tutor of the heir apparent and promoted to academy bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he made tutor of the heir apparent and then academy bachelor.

sentences.zh: 先後典福建、廣西鄉試，督河南、浙江、四川學政。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations of Fujian and Guangxi and served as educational commissioner of Henan, Zhejiang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Fujian and Guangxi provincial examinations in turn and served as educational commissioner of Henan, Zhejiang, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 所行皆本功令，律下尤嚴。

translations.literal: In all his conduct he followed the examination regulations, and was especially strict in enforcing discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He governed strictly by the examination regulations and was especially severe in enforcing discipline.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮戰事起，我師出平壤。

translations.literal: When the Korean war broke out, our army advanced to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Korea, Chinese forces advanced on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨上四路進兵之策，請兼募沿海漁人蜑戶編為舟師，使敵備多力分，庶可制勝。

translations.literal: Hongji memorialized a strategy of advancing by four routes and requested also recruiting coastal fishermen and boat people into naval forces, so that the enemy would prepare on many fronts and divide its strength, and victory might thereby be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji proposed a four-pronged advance and urged recruiting coastal fishermen and boat people into naval units to spread the enemy thin and divide its strength, hoping thereby to win.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，鴻禨方自蜀還，復奏言秦中地形險要，請豫建陪都。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, Hongji had just returned from Sichuan and again memorialized that the terrain of Qin was strategically vital, requesting that a secondary capital be built in advance.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was settled, Hongji had just returned from Sichuan and memorialized that the Qin region's terrain was strategically vital, urging construction of a secondary capital in advance.

sentences.zh: 日本增兵遼東，鴻禨以敵情叵測，請敕劉坤一、王文韶簡練勁旅，不可專任淮軍。

translations.literal: When Japan reinforced troops in Liaodong, Hongji, because the enemy's intentions were unpredictable, requested an edict ordering Liu Kunyi and Wang Wenshao to select and train crack troops, and that the Huai army alone should not be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan reinforced Liaodong, Hongji—finding the enemy's intentions unpredictable—urged Liu Kunyi and Wang Wenshao to train crack troops and warned against relying solely on the Huai army.

sentences.zh: 適坤一奏劾山西將賀星明侵餉，革職，鴻禨言：「刑賞治天下之大柄，軍紀廢弛已久，宜嚴懲以儆其餘。

translations.literal: Just then Kunyi memorialized impeaching Shanxi General He Xingming for embezzling pay and had him dismissed; Hongji said: "Punishment and reward are the great handles by which the empire is governed; military discipline has long been lax, and severe punishment should be applied to warn the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Kunyi impeached Shanxi General He Xingming for embezzling pay and had him dismissed; Hongji argued: "Reward and punishment are the great levers of governance; military discipline has long collapsed, and severe punishment is needed to warn others.

sentences.zh: 」又：「葉志超、龔照嶼等敗軍辱國，罪當死。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ye Zhichao, Gong Zhaoyu, and others disgraced the nation by defeat; their crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Ye Zhichao, Gong Zhaoyu, and others disgraced the nation in defeat and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 和約既定，勢不能與勾，宜籍其財產，或令巨款捐贖，然後貸其一死。

translations.literal: Now that the peace treaty is fixed, it is impossible to execute them together; their property should be confiscated, or they should be made to pay a large sum as ransom, and then their lives may be spared.
translations.idiomatic: With peace settled, mass execution is no longer possible; their property should be confiscated, or they should pay a heavy ransom, and then their lives may be spared.

sentences.zh: 」皆不報。

translations.literal: None of these received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals received a response.

sentences.zh: 旋遷禮部侍郎，出督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and went out to supervise education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of Rites and sent out as educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 請罷武科。

translations.literal: He requested abolition of the military examination.
translations.idiomatic: He urged abolition of the military examination.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西狩，鴻禨差竣詣行在，道授左都御使，晉工部尚書，仍以西安陪都為言。

translations.literal: When the two palaces fled west, Hongji, upon completing his assignment, proceeded to the traveling palace; en route he was appointed left censor-in-chief and promoted to minister of the Ministry of Works, again urging Xi'an as a secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, Hongji finished his duties and hurried to join it; en route he was made left censor-in-chief and minister of Works, again urging Xi'an as a secondary capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，命直軍機，兼充政務處大臣。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was ordered to serve directly on the Grand Council and concurrently appointed minister of the Bureau of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he joined the Grand Council and served on the Bureau of Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 請以策論試士，開經濟特科，汰書吏，悉允行。

translations.literal: He requested examining scholars by policy discourse, opening a special economic examination, and reducing clerical runners; all were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed policy-essay examinations, a special economic examination, and reduction of clerical staff—all approved.

sentences.zh: 改總理各國事務衙門為外務部，班六部上，以鴻禨為尚書。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen for Managing the Affairs of All Nations was changed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranked above the Six Ministries, and Hongji was appointed minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongli Yamen was reorganized as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranked above the Six Ministries, with Hongji as its minister.

sentences.zh: 時方與各國議和，鴻禨治事明敏，諳究外交，承旨擬諭，語中竅要，頗當上意焉。

translations.literal: At that time peace was being negotiated with the various nations; Hongji handled affairs with keen intelligence, was thoroughly versed in foreign relations, drafted edicts according to imperial intent, and his language hit the vital points, greatly pleasing the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: While peace was being negotiated with foreign powers, Hongji handled affairs with sharp intelligence and deep knowledge of diplomacy; his drafted edicts hit the mark and greatly pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕回鑾，賞黃馬褂，加太子太保。

translations.literal: He escorted the court back to the capital, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and given the additional title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting the court home, he was granted the yellow jacket and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 自新政議起，興學、通商、勸工諸政，有司多藉端巧取。

translations.literal: Since the new policies were debated, in matters of establishing schools, promoting trade, and encouraging industry, local officials often used pretexts to extract funds by artifice.
translations.idiomatic: Once the New Policies were launched, local officials often used school-building, trade promotion, and industrial encouragement as pretexts for extortion.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨請降旨禁革苛派，任民間自辦。

translations.literal: Hongji requested an edict forbidding harsh levies and allowing the people to manage affairs themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji sought an edict banning harsh levies and allowing people to manage affairs themselves.

sentences.zh: 又請旨以戶部正雜諸款供地方正用，宮中歲費，遵先朝定例，量入為出，不便自戶部增撥。

translations.literal: He also requested an edict that regular and miscellaneous funds of the Ministry of Revenue should supply local regular expenses, that the palace's annual expenditures should follow the fixed precedents of former reigns, spending according to income, and that it was not convenient to increase allocations from the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that regular and miscellaneous revenue fund local expenses, that palace expenditures follow former precedents with spending matched to income, and that the Ministry of Revenue should not increase palace allocations.

sentences.zh: 裁汰內務府冗員，用節糜費。

translations.literal: He reduced redundant staff in the Imperial Household Department to save wasteful expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He cut redundant staff in the Imperial Household Department to curb waste.

sentences.zh: 充中日議約全權大臣。

translations.literal: He served as plenipotentiary minister for negotiating the Sino-Japanese treaty.
translations.idiomatic: He served as plenipotentiary for the Sino-Japanese treaty negotiations.

sentences.zh: 是時中外咸以立憲為請，朝廷下詔豫備憲政始基，勗天下以忠君尊孔、尚公尚武尚實，用鴻禨言也。

translations.literal: At that time both at home and abroad all requested constitutional government; the court issued an edict preparing the foundation of constitutional government, exhorting the empire to loyalty to the ruler and reverence for Confucius, and to valuing public spirit, martial spirit, and practicality—following Hongji's words.
translations.idiomatic: When constitutional government was widely urged at home and abroad, the court issued an edict laying the groundwork for constitutional rule, exhorting the empire to loyalty, Confucian reverence, public spirit, martial virtue, and practicality—following Hongji's counsel.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he became associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he became associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 特旨派議改官制大臣，鴻禨以樞廷事冗辭。

translations.literal: By special edict he was appointed a minister to deliberate on reform of the official system; Hongji declined on the grounds that Grand Council affairs were too numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict he was named to deliberate on bureaucratic reform, but Hongji declined, citing the press of Grand Council business.

sentences.zh: 旋命與大學士孫家鼐复核，頗有裁正焉。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to review the proposals jointly with Grand Secretary Sun Jianai, and made many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to review the proposals with Grand Secretary Sun Jianai and made substantial corrections.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨持躬清刻，以儒臣驟登政地，銳於任事。

translations.literal: Hongji conducted himself with austere integrity; as a Confucian minister suddenly elevated to political power, he was keen to take on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji lived with austere integrity; a Confucian scholar suddenly thrust into power, he was eager to take charge.

sentences.zh: 素善岑春煊，春煊入朝，留長郵傳部。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Cen Chunxuan; when Chunxuan entered the capital, he was retained as head of the Ministry of Posts and Communications.
