translations.idiomatic: He had long been allied with Cen Chunxuan, who on entering the capital was kept on as head of the Ministry of Posts and Communications.

sentences.zh: 密疏劾慶親王奕劻，奕劻惡春煊，遂及鴻禨。

translations.literal: He secretly memorialized impeaching Prince Qing Yikuang; Yikuang hated Chunxuan, and thus Hongji was implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly impeached Prince Qing Yikuang; Yikuang hated Cen Chunxuan, and Hongji was dragged down with him.

sentences.zh: 會鴻禨因直言忤太后旨，侍講學士惲毓鼎劾以攬權恣縱，遂罷斥歸里。

translations.literal: When Hongji, because of blunt speech, offended the Empress Dowager's will, Expositor of the Hanlin Academy Yun Yuding impeached him for monopolizing power and acting willfully, and he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongji's blunt speech offended the Empress Dowager, Expositor Yun Yuding impeached him for monopolizing power, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，湘變起，流寓上海，旋卒。

translations.literal: In the xinhai year the Hunan disturbance broke out; he lived in exile in Shanghai and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911, as upheaval spread in Hunan, he took refuge in Shanghai and soon died.

sentences.zh: 後追諡文慎。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously given the title Wenshen.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously granted the title Wenshen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：德宗親政，憤於外侮，思變法自強。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When Emperor Dezong personally took power, he was indignant at foreign insult and thought of reforming the laws to strengthen the state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When Emperor Guangxu took personal rule, he burned with indignation at foreign humiliation and sought reform to strengthen the state.

sentences.zh: 乃以輔導無人，戊戌黨禍，庚子匪亂，遂相繼而作。

translations.literal: Yet because there was no one to guide him, the party disaster of the wuxu year and the Boxer disturbance of the gengzi year followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: But lacking able counselors, the Hundred Days' catastrophe of 1898 and the Boxer uprising of 1900 followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 太后再出垂簾，初堅復舊，繼勉圖新。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager again came forth to hold the curtain regency; at first she firmly restored the old ways, then strove to pursue the new.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager resumed regency, at first firmly restoring the old order, then pushing toward reform.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，議行憲政。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong reign was proclaimed, constitutional government was debated and undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuantong reign, constitutional government was debated and launched.

sentences.zh: 政體既變，國本遂搖，而大勢不可問矣。

translations.literal: Once the political system changed, the foundation of the state was shaken, and the great trend could no longer be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Once the political system shifted, the foundations of the state shook, and the larger course of events was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 榮祿屢參大變，文韶久達世務。

translations.literal: Rong Lu repeatedly participated in great upheavals; Wenshao long understood affairs of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu weathered repeated upheavals; Wenshao had long mastered affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨後起，參議立憲，終以失寵太后，不免放斥。

translations.literal: Hongji rose later, participated in deliberating constitutional government, but in the end lost favor with the Empress Dowager and could not escape dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji rose later and helped shape constitutional plans, but ultimately lost the Empress Dowager's favor and was cast out.

sentences.zh: 唯之洞一時稱賢，而監國攝政，親貴用事，欲挽救而未能，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: Only Zhidong was for a time called worthy; yet under the regency of the supervising prince, imperial kin held power, he wished to save the situation but could not, and thus died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhidong was hailed as the ablest man of his day; yet under the regent prince, imperial kin held sway, and though he tried to save the situation he could not, and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁，尚何言哉？

translations.literal: When worthy men perish, the state is brought to ruin—what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men are gone, the state lies in ruins—what more can be said?
